metaDescription: Five cordless circular saws under $150, from a 4-1/2 inch mini to a 6-1/2 inch Milwaukee bare tool, with cut depth, blade size and battery reality compared.
expertTake: The DEWALT DCS391B is the pick if you already own 20V MAX batteries, because it pairs a magnesium shoe and a 5150 rpm motor with a battery family you can grow into. The DEKOPRO 6-1/2 inch kit is the value pick for someone starting from scratch, since it ships with two packs and a charger. Skip the 4-1/2 inch and 5-1/2 inch mini saws if you cut 2x lumber, because their depth at 45 degrees falls below the thickness of a 2x4.
introParagraphs: A cordless circular saw trades a cord for a battery, and the blade diameter, motor type and pack size decide whether it cuts framing lumber or only trim and plywood. The marketing numbers, from rpm to voltage, describe the motor and say little about how deep the blade reaches.

This guide explains what a spending cap of $150 buys, what you give up against a pricier brushless saw, and how to read depth, speed and battery figures. Our top picks are above, with full reviews below. Prices move, and the cap reflects listing prices when this guide was updated.

products.name: DEWALT DCS391B 20V MAX 6-1/2 in Cordless Circular Saw, Tool Only
products.description:
The DCS391B is a sidewinder saw, meaning the motor sits beside the blade and spins it through a direct gear. A 5150 rpm motor on a 6-1/2 inch blade gives a blade tip speed fast enough to cut dimensional lumber cleanly, and a lightweight magnesium shoe keeps the base flat and accurate over years of dragging across boards.

It is sold as a bare tool, so you must supply a 20V MAX battery and charger. If you already own DEWALT packs, this is among the best buys in the roundup. If you do not, the DEKOPRO kit gives you two packs for a similar total outlay. Against the Milwaukee 2630-20, which is also bare, the DEWALT has a higher rpm and a lighter body, while the Milwaukee uses a larger 18V battery system with brushless options.

Upkeep is straightforward: clean the blade guard so it snaps closed, replace the blade when the teeth dull and wipe sawdust from the shoe. A 6-1/2 inch blade is cheap and widely stocked. Fit a thin-kerf 24 tooth blade for framing and a 40 tooth blade for plywood, because the stock blade is a compromise.
products.bestFor: DEWALT battery owners who want a reliable framing and plywood saw.
pros: 5150 rpm 6-1/2 inch blade cuts dimensional lumber cleanly
Lightweight magnesium shoe keeps the base flat and accurate
Rubber overmolded grip gives control during long cuts
Broad 20V MAX platform makes the next tool cheaper
cons: Sold as a bare tool, so battery and charger cost extra
Brushed motor wastes more battery than a brushless saw
Cut depth is less than a 7-1/4 inch corded saw

products.name: DEKOPRO 20V Cordless Circular Saw, 6-1/2 in, 4500 rpm
products.description:
The DEKOPRO is the only 6-1/2 inch saw here that ships ready to cut, with two batteries and a charger in the box. A 4500 rpm blade speed is below the DEWALT's 5150 rpm, which means slightly slower cutting but also lower strain on the pack. A pair of batteries lets you swap packs and keep working, a feature that matters on a deck or fence project.

The listing is vague on depth of cut and bevel capacity, so treat the saw as a general-purpose tool and measure its depth with a ruler before you rely on it for 2x4 framing at 45 degrees. A 6-1/2 inch blade usually cuts about 2 inches at 90 degrees, enough for 2x lumber at square cuts. Compared with the KARTOP mini, it is a bigger saw with a deeper cut.

The tradeoff is the platform: the DEKOPRO packs fit few other tools. Keep the guard clean, replace blades when they burn the cut and store the packs indoors. Because 6-1/2 inch blades are stocked at every hardware store, replacement costs stay low even on a lesser known saw.
products.bestFor: Beginners who want a saw, two packs and a charger in one box.
pros: Two batteries and a charger included, so it cuts out of the box
6-1/2 inch blade reaches through 2x lumber at square cuts
4500 rpm is fast enough for plywood and dimensional lumber
Ergonomic handle reduces hand fatigue on long cuts
cons: Depth and bevel capacity are not stated clearly
Small platform with few other tools to add
Slower blade speed than the DEWALT

products.name: Milwaukee M18 2630-20 6-1/2 in Cordless Circular Saw, Bare Tool
products.description:
The 2630-20 is a professional-grade saw with a 3500 rpm motor, magnesium upper and lower guards and a soft grip, built to tolerate being dropped off a truck tailgate. The slower blade speed than the DEWALT is deliberate: a bigger torque curve means it keeps its speed when it hits an LVL header, which the maker names as a typical job.

Like the DEWALT, it is a bare tool, which means a battery and charger are an extra. Milwaukee's M18 platform is one of the largest in the trade, so if you already own M18 packs, this is a strong buy. If you do not, it is a hard sell against the kit-style DEKOPRO. Against the DEWALT, the Milwaukee's magnesium guards give it a more durable lower guard, a part that cracks on cheaper saws.

Expect many years of service. Keep the guards clean, replace brushes if the saw smells hot, and use thin-kerf blades to save battery. Owners working around concrete forms should keep the rafter-style hook habits in mind, since hanging a running saw is an invitation to kickback.
products.bestFor: M18 owners who want a durable saw for regular framing work.
pros: Magnesium upper and lower guards resist cracks and drops
Maintains speed through dense LVL header material
Soft grip stays comfortable over long cuts
Part of the large M18 battery platform
cons: Sold as a bare tool with no battery or charger
3500 rpm is slower than the DEWALT on thin sheet goods
Highest cost of entry among the 6-1/2 inch saws here

products.name: KARTOP 5-1/2 in Brushless Mini Circular Saw, 7000 rpm Kit
products.description:
KARTOP squeezes a brushless motor and a 7000 rpm spindle into a 4.19 pound body with a 5-1/2 inch blade. The stated depth of 2-3/16 inch at 90 degrees clears a standard 2x, but at 45 degrees it falls to 1-7/16 inch, which is thinner than the 1-1/2 inch thickness of a 2x4, so a bevel cut through framing lumber will not go all the way through.

Two 4000 mAh packs and three blades make it a complete kit. The tradeoff is the platform and the saw's role: it is a trim, plywood and decking saw, not a framing tool. Compared with the GALAX PRO's 4-1/2 inch blade, it has a bigger blade and deeper cut, and against the DEKOPRO 6-1/2 inch it is lighter and quicker on thin stock but cuts less depth.

The low weight is its best feature for overhead and one-handed cuts. Keep the packs charged, replace the blades with a fine-tooth type for plywood and watch the depth setting. Plywood users should pair it with a 40 tooth or finer blade to avoid tear-out on the top face.
products.bestFor: Plywood, decking and trim where a light, quick saw beats a full-size one.
pros: Brushless 7000 rpm motor cuts thin stock quickly and cleanly
Two 4000 mAh packs and three blades included
4.19 lb body is easy to control one-handed
2-3/16 inch depth at 90 degrees clears a 2x at square cuts
cons: 1-7/16 inch depth at 45 degrees will not clear a 2x4 on a bevel
Mini 5-1/2 inch blade is not a framing saw
Small platform with no wider tool range

products.name: GALAX PRO 20V 4-1/2 in Cordless Mini Circular Saw with Laser
products.description:
The GALAX PRO is the smallest saw in the roundup, a 4-1/2 inch mini with 1-11/16 inch of depth at 90 degrees and 1-1/8 inch at 45. That is plenty for trim, laminate flooring, thin plywood, plastic and soft metals, but it will not cut through a 2x4 in a single pass at 90 degrees, which needs 1-1/2 inch and just clears.

A laser guide helps keep a parallel line on long rips, and two blades come in the box. The 2.0 Ah pack is the smallest in the group, which means short run time and a recharge on larger jobs. Against the KARTOP, it is cheaper and lighter but cuts shallower and spins slower at 3400 rpm.

Treat it as a craft and hobby saw. Clamp the work, use the blade type matched to the material and do not force the cut, since a small motor overheats quickly. A square and a clamped straightedge will do more for accuracy than the laser on a saw this small.
products.bestFor: Crafts, trim, laminate and thin sheet goods where a tiny saw is enough.
pros: Laser guide keeps long cuts on a straight line
4-1/2 inch blade suits laminate, trim and thin plywood
Two blades included for wood and soft materials
Light enough to use one-handed on small pieces
cons: 1-1/8 inch depth at 45 degrees is very shallow
2.0 Ah pack runs flat quickly under load
Not suited to framing lumber or thick stock

buyingCriteria.explanation: Depth of cut equals blade radius minus the shoe and arbor, and bevel cuts reduce it further. A 6-1/2 inch blade cuts about 2 inches at 90 degrees, and a 4-1/2 inch blade cuts under 1-3/4 inch. The KARTOP at 1-7/16 inch at 45 degrees and the GALAX PRO at 1-1/8 inch fall below the 1-1/2 inch thickness of a 2x4, so check this number before you buy. The rule of thumb is that your saw must cut at least a quarter inch deeper than the stock, so the blade clears the bottom face and the teeth exit cleanly.

A brushless motor runs cooler and gets more cuts from each charge, which matters because a saw drains a battery faster than a drill. The KARTOP lists a brushless motor, and the DEWALT DCS391B and DEKOPRO are brushed designs. If you cut every weekend, brushless pays off, and for occasional use brushed is fine. A brushed saw such as the DEKOPRO can still finish a deck, but expect to swap packs more often.

A bare tool is cheaper only if you already own batteries and a charger. The DEWALT and Milwaukee saws here are bare, so a new buyer must add a pack and charger. The DEKOPRO and KARTOP ship with two packs, which makes them the easier starting points.

A higher rpm cuts thin stock faster, and a lower rpm with more torque holds up in dense lumber. The KARTOP at 7000 rpm and the DEWALT at 5150 rpm suit plywood and framing, while the Milwaukee at 3500 rpm is built for LVL headers. Match the speed to the material. A saw with high rpm and a weak motor bogs down in wet lumber, so slow your feed rate rather than forcing the cut.

A 20V MAX or M18 platform lets you add tools later at bare-tool prices. The DEWALT and Milwaukee sit on large platforms, while the KARTOP, GALAX PRO and DEKOPRO sit on small ones. If you plan to build a collection, the platform is worth more than a faster blade.

The lower blade guard must snap closed, and the shoe must stay flat. Magnesium shoes and guards, like on the DEWALT and Milwaukee, resist bending, while stamped steel and plastic parts on cheap saws bend after a drop. A bent shoe causes cuts that wander.

specDecoder.meaning: Blade speed with no resistance. Under load, speed falls, so the figure shows potential rather than performance.
specDecoder.watchFor: The KARTOP's 7000 rpm is on a small blade, so tip speed is comparable to a larger saw at lower rpm. Rpm alone does not set cut quality, so tooth count and blade kerf matter equally.

specDecoder.meaning: The deepest cut when the base is tilted. It is always less than the 90 degree depth.
specDecoder.watchFor: The KARTOP's 1-7/16 inch and the GALAX PRO's 1-1/8 inch fall short of a 2x4's 1-1/2 inch.

specDecoder.meaning: A tool sold without a battery or charger. It is cheaper if you own a compatible platform.
specDecoder.watchFor: The DEWALT DCS391B and Milwaukee 2630-20 are bare, so add the pack and charger cost.

specDecoder.meaning: The pack's electrical pressure. The 20V MAX label is the peak and the nominal value is about 18V.
specDecoder.watchFor: Labels such as 21V on the KARTOP describe a similar class, so compare motor and battery size instead.

specDecoder.meaning: Battery capacity, with 4000 mAh equal to 4.0 Ah. A larger figure means more cuts per charge.
specDecoder.watchFor: The GALAX PRO's 2.0 Ah pack holds half the energy of the KARTOP's 4.0 Ah packs.

howWeEvaluated.title: Depth of cut
howWeEvaluated.description: We began with what each saw can cut. The three 6-1/2 inch saws reach about 2 inches at square cuts, the KARTOP reaches 2-3/16 inch and the GALAX PRO reaches 1-11/16 inch.

howWeEvaluated.title: Motor and speed
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared rpm and motor type. The KARTOP's brushless 7000 rpm is the fastest, and the Milwaukee's 3500 rpm is the most torque-oriented.

howWeEvaluated.title: Battery and kit contents
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered what ships in the box. The DEKOPRO and KARTOP include two packs, and the DEWALT and Milwaukee are bare.

howWeEvaluated.title: Build quality
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at the shoe and guard materials. The DEWALT magnesium shoe and the Milwaukee magnesium guards led.

howWeEvaluated.title: Owner feedback patterns
howWeEvaluated.description: We noted recurring themes such as bent shoes and battery fade. Lesser known labels were scored cautiously on parts support.

howToChoose.intro: Start with the thickest stock you cut, because depth at the bevel angle you use decides which saws are even eligible.

howToChoose.note: Pick a mini saw for sheet goods and trim. Pick a 6-1/2 inch saw if you cut framing lumber.

howToChoose.intro: Platform lock-in is the long term cost here, because each extra tool reuses the packs you already bought.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: At least 2 inch depth at 90 degrees, two batteries and a blade for dimensional lumber. A bevel capacity of 45 degrees helps with angled cuts.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The DEKOPRO and DEWALT fit best. The KARTOP suits decking boards, and the Milwaukee suits heavy lumber.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You cut framing every week. A 7-1/4 inch brushless saw outlasts the DEWALT DCS391B and DEKOPRO.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You cut plywood and trim now and then. The KARTOP or GALAX PRO does that.

maintenance.why: A dull blade overloads the motor and drains the pack. A sharp blade makes cleaner cuts and extends battery life.
Sawdust jams the guard so it will not close. A stuck guard is a safety hazard.
A bent shoe makes the saw cut off line. Replace or return a saw with a bent shoe.
Heat and cold shorten pack life. Store at about half charge.
Worn brushes cause weak power and sparking. The DEWALT and DEKOPRO are the models to check.

faq.q: Can a cordless circular saw replace a corded one?
faq.a: For most home projects, yes. A corded 7-1/4 inch saw still cuts deeper and runs without limit, while a cordless saw suits mobility, roof work and jobs far from an outlet.

faq.q: What does $150 buy in a cordless circular saw?
faq.a: A 6-1/2 inch brushed saw, either as a bare tool or a kit, or a brushless mini saw. You give up brushless power and a deep cut. The cap reflects listing prices when this guide was updated.

faq.q: Can a mini saw cut a 2x4?
faq.a: At square cuts, a 5-1/2 inch saw can. At 45 degrees, depth falls below 1-1/2 inch, so it will not cut through.

faq.q: Is brushless worth it for a saw?
faq.a: If you cut often, yes, because it gets more cuts per charge. For occasional use, a brushed saw is fine.

faq.q: Should I buy a bare tool?
faq.a: Only if you own compatible batteries and a charger. Otherwise, a kit is cheaper overall.

Yes. Wear eye and ear protection, clamp the work and keep both hands clear of the blade path. Let the blade reach full speed before the cut and release the trigger before lifting the saw out of the kerf.
